18:T9b1, Sharing Files to Your Project Submission Page The Project page DOES allow for the upload or copy/paste of images (JPG, PNG, GIF up to 10MB). However, it DOES NOT allow for the upload of videos or documents. Including Videos or Documents in Your Project Submission: Upload your files to a cloud service or repository (e.g., YouTube, Google Drive, GitHub, OneDrive, Dropbox, etc.) and share a publicly accessible link with no logins, permissions, or registrations required. If judges canât access your project, it canât be evaluated or judged. Most platforms have a âshareâ option that provides a URL. Before submitting: Set the file to public access Test the link in a private browser or with teammates to confirm it works. Youâre welcome to link to a slide deck, video, or other visual aids. For additional tools and resources, see the Global Collaborators page. If you created a new website to host your project, we recommend requesting a Web Filter Classification to help ensure that judges can access your website. Please follow these steps: Complete the FortiGuard Web Filter Classification form . Fill in required fields. Please note: Category: You will need to select a category that best describes your site. This could include education, personal website and blogs, reference, or web-based application. NASA Space Apps is unable to make the categorization determination for you, so select the one from the choices in the form that best describes your final project. Company Name: Write âN/Aâ Submit your request for classification. While this is not required for project submission, requesting a classification can help prevent potential website access issues during judging. Please note: the categorization of sites is ultimately at Fortiguardâs discretion and NASA Space Apps has no direct influence. 19:T693, Did you utilize any Super Intelligence (SI) tools and software in preparing your solution?
